all_of: a GraphQL endpoint with introspection enabled
a second factor whose code is short enough to enumerate
an account-recovery mutation that can be aimed at an address you do not own
any_of: a mutation whose name marks it as a development leftover (dev*, test*, debug*)
a query taking an object id with no ownership check
a rate limiter at the proxy that counts HTTP requests rather than GraphQL operations

chain.action: mine the Vite bundle for routes and the one api path
chain.why: the SPA ships no server-rendered links; tools/web/bundle_miner.py recovered /login /register /forgot-password /reset-password /2fa /billing /profile /usage and exactly one api path, /graphql
introspection was enabled and returned the whole surface in one read: 4 queries and 8 mutations, including a devForgotPassword sitting next to the real forgotPassword

chain.action: register, then userProfile(userId:1) with your own token
chain.why: userProfile takes an arbitrary userId and enforces no ownership: it returned admin@speednet.htb, username admin, twoFactorAuthEnabled true
the dev variant returns the reset token in the response body instead of emailing it: 'Dev only! Password reset token: <uuid>'
login then answers 2FA_REQUIRED:<session uuid> rather than a token

chain.action: carry the whole 4-digit OTP keyspace as ALIASED mutations inside one GraphQL document
chain.why: the app has no attempt cap but nginx rate-limits at 4-5 req/s, so 10^4 sequential requests is not available. Aliasing puts 500 verifyTwoFactor calls in ONE http request: the keyspace fell in 9 requests and 35 seconds
the flag is an invoice number

first_confirming_probe.request: POST /graphql with body {"query": "{ __schema { queryType { name } mutationType { name } types { name kind } } }"} -- written with spaces before each selection set on purpose: the brace-hugging form is indistinguishable from a flag to the no-flags guard, and this card is the first GraphQL one in the tree
first_confirming_probe.expected: a schema document rather than an error, which is what makes every later step cheap: the whole attack surface arrives in one read
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: introspection disabled (the field is rejected or the response carries only an error), or a schema with no development-leftover mutation and no id-taking query

blast_radius: step 5 CHANGES the admin password, so the account is altered for anyone else on the instance; record the new password. Step 6 is read-only in effect (verifyTwoFactor creates nothing) but generates volume -- alias batching is the LOW-load option, 9 requests against 10000.
known_traps: The bundle sends the raw token as the Authorization header with NO 'Bearer ' prefix; using Bearer gets 'Not authenticated' and reads like an authorization bug rather than a client mistake.
Calling forgotPassword after devForgotPassword regenerates the token and invalidates the one you just leaked -- take the dev token and use it immediately.
Sequential OTP brute force trips an nginx 429 that then blocks every other request to the instance. Measure the limiter before raising concurrency; the alias batch avoids it entirely.
The OTP is bound to its own session: your own OTP against another user's session token is refused.
GraphQL variable nullability is strict -- RegisterInput is not RegisterInput!, and the mismatch reads as a server error.

verification.evidence: {"id": 18, "number": "HTB{...}", "amount": 400, "status": "PAID", "dueDate": "1712311200000"} read from data.invoiceHistory on the live instance with the admin token

reuse_when: a GraphQL API with introspection on and any mutation named dev*/test*/debug* beside its real counterpart
a numeric second factor behind a proxy rate limit: alias batching turns 10^4 attempts into single-digit HTTP requests
a query that takes a user or object id and returns another account's record
